chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left a male slave, and some of his sons testified that their father had freed him, he said: 'His testimony is accepted, and he is not penalized (for the value of the slave), and the slave is compensated from the estate for what was due to the other heirs.'

key_terms.أَعْتَقَهُ: He freed him (emancipation of a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's freedom if the owner dies and his sons claim he was freed?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural validity of a son's testimony regarding his father's emancipation of a slave during the final illness (*marad al-maut*). It establishes that the slave's value is treated as a debt against the estate, thereby compensating the other heirs without penalizing the testifying son personally, a nuance critical in Shia inheritance jurisprudence.
